hook: A thin conformal iridium oxide film on TiO2 cuts iridium use by about 84% in water electrolyzers
hook_turn: cuts iridium use by about 84% in water electrolyzers

readout.label: Reduction in iridium use vs commercial IrO2

summary: Iridium is scarce, and thinning it out usually breaks the electron pathways in the catalyst layer. Here a negatively charged TiOx surface steers iridium into a flat film instead of clumps, keeping conduction intact at 0.166 mg per cm2. Performance matched commercial IrO2, but the abstract reports no long-term durability test.
title: Interfacial Confinement Enables Conformal IrOx Nanofilms for Low-Ir-Loading PEM Water Electrolysis
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
